Evaluation Set-up: Trained on WMT 2014 datasets using two configurations: a base model trained for 100,000 steps (approximately 12 hours) and a big model trained for 300,000 steps (3.5 days) on a single machine with 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs.

Used Adam optimizer (β1=0.9, β2=0.98, ϵ=10^-9) with a learning rate schedule that warms up for 4000 steps, applied dropout (0.1 for base; 0.1 or 0.3 for big in different settings) and label smoothing (ϵ_ls = 0.1).

Batched sentence pairs by approximate sequence length with byte-pair encoding for English-German (≈4.5M sentence pairs, vocabulary ~37,000 tokens) and word-piece tokenization for English-French (36M sentence pairs, 32,000 vocabulary).
Employed beam search during inference (beam size 4 with length penalty α=0.6 for translation tasks and beam size 21 with extended maximum output length for constituency parsing).
For parsing experiments, used a 4-layer Transformer on the WSJ portion of the Penn Treebank, adjusting the maximum output length to input length + 300.
Benchmark evaluated on: English constituency parsing on the WSJ portion of the Penn Treebank
Expected Results: Transformer (big) achieves a new state-of-the-art BLEU score of 28.4 on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, outperforming previous models (including ensembles) by over 2 BLEU.

On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task, the Transformer establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 (with one report of 41.0 BLEU in experimental details), at a fraction of the training cost of previous models.

In English constituency parsing, the Transformer attains competitive performance with a 91.3 F1 score on the WSJ-only setting and 92.7 F1 in a semi-supervised setting, surpassing most previous models except the Recurrent Neural Network Grammar.
